country.name: Turkey
country.kicker: Where continents meet, history stays close.

overview.summary: A republic built from the heartland of the Ottoman Empire. Turkey’s position between the Black Sea, Europe, and the Middle East makes its geography inseparable from its politics and identity.
overview.geography: Most of Turkey lies on the Anatolian peninsula in Asia; a smaller part is in southeastern Europe. Istanbul straddles the Bosphorus. Ankara, inland, is the capital.

whyItMatters.title: A passage with strategic weight
whyItMatters.text: The Turkish Straits connect the Black Sea to the Mediterranean system, giving a narrow waterway international importance.

whyItMatters.title: Many worlds in one place
whyItMatters.text: Ottoman inheritances, a secular republican tradition, and a diverse society shape a country closely connected to both Europe and Asia.

sources.title: The Turkish Straits

stories.summary: For a Black Sea ship heading to the Mediterranean, geography offers a very particular path.

sections.title: A chain of passages
sections.text: The Bosphorus leads to the Sea of Marmara, then the Dardanelles and Aegean. Together these waters connect the Black Sea with the wider Mediterranean.

sections.title: Location meets law
sections.text: The Montreux Convention governs passage, with different rules for merchant vessels and warships. Geography gives Turkey leverage, but not unlimited discretion.

stories.takeaway: Some of the world’s most important connections are far narrower than the places they connect.

stories.summary: The modern state emerged after war and the collapse of an imperial order.

sections.title: An empire spanning regions
sections.text: The Ottoman Empire ruled lands across southeastern Europe, the Middle East, and North Africa at different times. Istanbul was its capital from 1453.

sections.title: A new center of gravity
sections.text: The Republic of Turkey was founded in 1923 under Mustafa Kemal Atatürk. Ankara became the capital, and reforms recast law, education, and public life.

stories.takeaway: Modern Turkey inherits an imperial past while being built around a very different idea of the state.

scene.mapNote: An inland capital shifted political focus away from imperial Istanbul.

stories.summary: The map answers one question. People’s lives answer many more.

sections.title: A literal crossing
sections.text: The straits separate Turkey’s smaller European territory from Anatolia. But continental labels are conventions, not complete explanations of culture.

sections.title: Overlapping connections
sections.text: Trade, migration, religion, language, and history connect Turkey to several regions. Its people hold varied identities and political views within those connections.

stories.takeaway: “Both” is a starting point, not the whole story.
